name: SIERRA LEONE
lead: Sierra Leone is on the coast of West Africa. Rainforest meets white Atlantic beaches here. The capital, Freetown, was founded by freed slaves in 1787. Red soil hides some of the world's finest diamonds.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Thick rainforest covers the east. Rolling hills in the north rise to Mount Bintumani. White-sand beaches line the coast.
Freetown sits on one of the world's largest natural deep-water harbours. The ancient Gola Rainforest in the south-east is millions of years old.
animals: More than 5,500 western chimpanzees live in Sierra Leone's forests, the second-largest wild group in the world.
The pygmy hippopotamus lives along the Moa River. It weighs just 200 kg and lives alone. The Gola malimbe, a red-and-black weaver bird, is found almost nowhere else.
culture: Krio, a mixed language born from English, African languages and Caribbean speech, joins all of Sierra Leone's peoples. Afrobeat, reggae and palm-wine guitar fill Freetown's streets.
Rice is part of every meal, with stew, groundnut soup or cassava-leaf sauce. In August, the Freetown Carnival fills the streets with colour and drumming.
history: In 1787, British anti-slavery campaigners settled freed Black people on the 'Province of Freedom', the start of Freetown. After Britain banned the slave trade in 1807, thousands more freed Africans arrived.
Diamonds found in 1930 brought wealth and conflict. A civil war from 1991 to 2002, paid for by 'blood diamonds', killed 50,000 people. Sierra Leone has rebuilt since.
wows: The 969-carat Star of Sierra Leone (1972) is the largest river-gravel diamond ever found.
Freetown's harbour is so deep that the world's largest ships can anchor without touching the seabed.
Freed slaves prayed under the city's 300-year-old Cotton Tree in 1792.
Krio sounds so close to English that many English speakers can partly understand it.
Tacugama Sanctuary has cared for over 100 chimps and freed some into the forest.
Tokeh and River No. 2 Beach are among Africa's most beautiful, yet barely visited.
Half of Sierra Leone's people are under 19, one of the world's youngest nations.

myths.myth: Sierra Leone is named after real lions
myths.fact: Portuguese explorer Pedro de Sintra named the hills 'Serra Lyoa' (Lion Mountains) in 1462. Some say thunder there sounded like roaring lions.
Diamonds form deep in the Earth, far below any coal. Most are over a billion years old.
